Palm Springs, California · off the bike

Palm Springs off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars

What to do in Palm Springs with the afternoon after the ride and the evening before it. A short list, not a city guide: the record store, the bookshop, the bar, the market.

Palm Springs off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars, listed

  1. Palm Springs Aerial Tramway

    1 Tram Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, the top of Tramway Road. The rotating tram car from the Valley Station to the Mountain Station at 8,516 feet, about ten minutes up, by the visitor bureau's guide: the rider who climbed Tramway Road wants to see the top, and the one who didn't gets 8,500 feet and snow in February. Adults $36.95 (its tickets page, Oct 2026, with the $2 online fee); winter hours Oct 5, 2026 to May 27, 2027 are first car up 10 a.m. weekdays and 8 a.m. weekends, last car up 8 p.m., last down 9:30 p.m. Parking $15 a car, and it closes about a month each year for maintenance, usually September (visitpalmsprings.com, Sept 2026). Bikes stop at the toll gate below the station (see Routes).

  2. Palm Springs Swim Center

    405 S Pavilion Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, Sunrise Park, east of downtown off Sunrise Way: the city's outdoor pool, the swim after the ride. Drop-in swimming Monday to Thursday 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., Friday to Sunday 6 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Tuesdays 8 to 10 a.m. for maintenance; $10 a swim for a non-resident adult, $6 for residents (city page, Oct 2026). The pool's length isn't on the page; (760) 323-8278.

  3. Palm Springs Art Museum, Architecture and Design Center

    Museum · 300 S Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, on S Palm Canyon a block south of the Tour de Palm Springs start block, in E. Stewart Williams's 1961 glass-and-steel Santa Fe Federal Savings building, and the start of the Midcentury Modern loop (see Routes): architecture and design shows, two hours, the cheap way into the mid-century side of town. Open Thursday noon to 8, Friday to Sunday 10 to 5, closed Monday to Wednesday; $25, free Thursdays 5 to 8 p.m. (Oct 2026). The main museum (101 Museum Drive, two blocks west of Palm Canyon) keeps the same hours, price and free Thursday evening, per its own page.

  4. VillageFest

    Market · 100 S Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, downtown: the Thursday night street fair on Palm Canyon Drive, 180-plus vendors, arts, crafts, food, live entertainment, dog-friendly, shops open late, by its own page. Every Thursday, 6 to 10 p.m. October through May and 7 to 10 p.m. June through September (its venue page, Oct 2026). Palm Canyon closes to cars for it. Thursday, February 4, 2027 is the one before the Tour, on the street the Tour starts on two days later.

  5. Palm Springs Vinyl Records & Collectibles

    Record store · 220 N Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, downtown, on Palm Canyon Dr between Amadeo Rd and Tahquitz Canyon Way, a block north of the Tour start block. Records, CDs, cassettes, posters and music and movie collectibles; it buys as well as sells, and says it has been at it for over 40 years. Open 11 to 6, seven days a week, per its own site (read Oct 3, 2026).

  6. The Best Bookstore in Palm Springs

    Bookstore · 113 La Plaza, Palm Springs, CA

    Zone 1, downtown, in La Plaza off S Palm Canyon. Independent; its own site calls it a "family-owned bookstore with branches in Palm Springs and San Francisco." Publishers Weekly's piece on its opening names an LGBTQ section, a Spanish-language section, Native American authors, regional history and Palm Springs architecture. The city's visitor listing gives 10 to 6 every day; another directory lists shorter weekday hours, so call (760) 933-3619 before you walk over.

  7. The Shops at Thirteen Forty-Five

    1345 North Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, Uptown. The mid-century furniture and vintage stretch of N Palm Canyon runs north from Alejo Road, and this is the one-stop version of it: vintage and modern furniture, art, jewelry, resort wear, a bookstore and a café under one roof, by its own page. Open Thursday to Monday 10 to 6 (Oct 2026); (760) 464-0480. The other shops cluster in the 600 and 700 blocks (Modern Way 745, Bon Vivant 751, Iconic Atomic 724, per Visit Palm Springs, Dec 2025).

  8. Hunters

    Queer-owned · 302 E Arenas Rd, Palm Springs, CA 92262

    Zone 1, Arenas Road, downtown: the dance bar, two rooms (bar and pool tables; dance floor), a patio, DJs, drag, karaoke, bingo, watch parties, by its own site. Founded 1998 by Mark Hunter Seymour; its own About page says "LGBTQ+ owned, inclusive and welcoming." Open every day 10 a.m. to 2 a.m. (Oct 2026); (760) 323-0700. Streetbar is across the street for the quieter drink.

  9. Streetbar

    Bar · 224 E. Arenas Road, Palm Springs

    Zone 1, Arenas Road, downtown, across from Hunters. Opened in 1991 as the first gay bar in Palm Springs, per Palm Springs Life: a neighborhood bar with a patio, locals through the day and visitors at night and on weekends. Open 10 a.m. to 2 a.m. every day, per the city's visitor listing. The plain answer to where to get a drink after the ride.
